codeReview.summary: Clean, well-structured implementation of the contract runner in 127 lines. All functions are small with single responsibilities (checkAssertion, writeEvidenceFiles, shouldRunAssertion, runContractAssertions). Follows project conventions: import type for type-only imports, .js extensions, const usage, no comments, early returns, sync I/O consistent with state manager patterns. All 13 VAL requirements (VAL-RUNNER-001 through 008, 011-013, VAL-EVIDENCE-001, VAL-EVIDENCE-003) are covered by 24 well-structured tests using mock exec and temp directories. TDD workflow followed per transcript (red-green verified). Exit code, stdout contains/not-contains, stderr contains all correctly checked with short-circuit evaluation. Timeout handled as error status. Evidence files (stdout.log, stderr.log, result.json) written per assertion. Milestone feature filtering, skipped/blocked feature skipping, and contract status updates all correctly implemented.

issues.description: ExecFn type is imported from run-validation.ts, creating a coupling between the contract runner and the run-validation tool. If ExecFn were defined in types.ts or a shared module, it would reduce the bidirectional dependency. Currently run-validation imports from contract-runner and contract-runner imports from run-validation.

writeEvidenceFiles calls mkdirSync on every assertion execution, even though the directory is the same for all assertions in a single run. While harmless (mkdirSync with recursive:true is idempotent), it could be hoisted to the main loop for minor efficiency.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The ExecFn type is defined in run-validation.ts and imported by contract-runner.ts, while contract-runner.ts exports AssertionResult which is likely consumed by run-validation.ts. This creates a circular-ish import pattern. AGENTS.md and architecture.md don't document where shared types between tools should live (types.ts vs. co-located).
